headline: The new HRRR dropped its Friday-morning downpour (0.54 in in 3 hours down to almost nothing) and NBM also eased, so the consensus fell from 0.39 to 0.12 in: showers only, no street flooding expected.

summary.text: HRRR's 2 PM run removed the strong 4–6 AM Friday cell (0.54 in down to 0.02 in). NBM eased from 0.23 to 0.12 in. Consensus fell from 0.39 to 0.12 in.
Wettest 3 hours in the next 72 h: RRFS 0.39 in (older 4 AM run, the outlier), ECMWF 0.15, NBM 0.12, GFS 0.06, HRRR 0.02. Consensus (HRRR ×1.25 = 0.03, RRFS 0.39, NBM 0.12: middle value) 0.12 in.
Most likely no water beyond the gutters. Water on the sidewalk would take a surprise downpour; Yellow (garage) needs about 0.71 in in 3 hours or a 0.40 in hour, and no model is close.
A few showers tonight. The wettest hours most models agree on are roughly 3 to 10 AM Friday, all light. Another light round Saturday evening (RRFS) or Sunday afternoon (ECMWF).
Friday's 7.9 ft high at 8:32 AM runs about 9.9 ft on the NOAA Bay model (~2 ft surge), during the Friday-morning showers. Caltrain channel 0.13 ft and falling, far below Monitoring (2.8 ft).
No need to move cars. Clear drain grates if you haven't yet, and glance at the page between 4 and 9 AM Friday in case a cell pops up.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: The surface low has moved inland and the thunderstorm threat is shifting to the Central Valley. NWS San Francisco's 1:51 PM update keeps chances for showers near the coast and adjacent inland areas through Friday afternoon, with the thunderstorm chance under 5% on Friday, followed by cold mornings Friday and Saturday. A frontal boundary late Saturday morning is now expected to fizzle as it moves south from the North Bay, so NWS no longer expects widespread rain this weekend, just post-frontal showers into Monday morning. The next system to watch arrives Tuesday into Wednesday, with NWS mentioning 1 to 3 in for the North Bay and coastal ranges, and the king tides arrive with it.

sections.title: What changed and model trends
sections.text:
Since the 1:20 PM discussion, the new HRRR (2 PM run) dropped the strong cell it had at 4 to 6 AM Friday. Its hourly rain is now dry here except 0.016 in in the hour ending 4 AM Friday, so its wettest 3 hours fell from 0.54 in to 0.02 in. Its 15-minute output still shows a brief shower around 3:15 to 3:45 AM Friday (about 0.11 in) and another small one near 6:30 AM, about 0.13 in in its wettest 3 hours, which is still light. GFS no longer copies the HRRR cell and is down to 0.06 in.

NBM eased from 0.23 to 0.12 in, wettest about 3 to 6 AM Friday with no hour above 0.06 in. ECMWF came up slightly, from 0.07 to 0.15 in, about 4 to 7 AM Friday at 0.05 in per hour. RRFS is still the 4 AM run, with 0.39 in about 6 to 9 AM Friday and no hour above 0.15 in. It is now the wettest model and the oldest, so I give it less weight.

The dashboard's consensus (HRRR ×1.25 = 0.03, RRFS 0.39, NBM 0.12; middle value) is 0.12 in, down from 0.39 in. That fits a fading shower pattern. The HRRR's earlier jumps, a cell at 10 PM in one run and at 5 AM in the next, now gone, show it could not pin down any single cell. A surprise cell is still possible but much less likely than this morning.

Storm totals for the next 72 hours: RRFS 0.83 in, ECMWF 0.54, NBM 0.43, GFS 0.22, HRRR 0.02 (its run ends Saturday 10 AM). Most of the ECMWF and RRFS extra comes from light weekend showers.

sections.title: Tide and the channel
sections.text:
The Bay is still running about 2 ft above the predicted tide on NOAA's Bay model. Tonight's 6.2 ft high at 8:09 PM shows about 8.3 ft. The low at 2:07 AM Friday (1.6 ft predicted) stays near 3.4 ft. The tide then rises quickly through the Friday-morning showers, from about 4.5 ft at 4 AM to 8.7 ft at 7 AM on the model, and Friday's 7.9 ft high at 8:32 AM peaks near 9.9 ft. Friday evening's 6.4 ft high at 9:15 PM shows about 8.5 ft. Saturday's high is higher, 8.4 ft predicted at 9:06 AM, and Sunday's 8.8 ft at 9:42 AM; the Bay model run ends before those.

The Coastal Flood Advisory for the Bay shoreline continues until 11 AM Saturday, with up to 1.8 ft of surge, and NWS says the Bays may be upgraded to a Coastal Flood Warning as the king tides approach. High Bay water slows how fast the channel drains on these mornings, but with light rain that should not matter much.

Channel: the gauge upstream of Caltrain is back down to 0.13 ft at 4:03 PM after the midday bump to 0.76 ft, far below county Flood Monitoring (2.8 ft). At Alameda de las Pulgas it is 0.27 ft at 4 PM (Monitoring 3.18 ft).

sections.title: Current observations
sections.text: Mostly a break in the showers. The Caltrain rain gauge has not recorded rain since 0.04 in in the 1 PM hour (last tip 1:06 PM); 0.08 in over the last 6 hours and 0.44 in over 24 hours. Both channel gauges are low and steady or falling.

sections.title: Uncertainty
sections.text: Low. The models now agree that only light showers are left, and the one model that showed a strong cell has dropped it. The remaining wildcard is a lone shower cell over a few blocks early Friday, when the ground is wet and the high tide with about 2 ft of surge is coming in, but even the wettest model (RRFS, 0.39 in in 3 hours) is well under the Yellow line. Most likely outcome: no street flooding.

sections.title: What to do
sections.text:
• No need to move cars out of the cul-de-sac.
• If you haven't already, clear leaves from the street drain grates and yard drains; more rain is likely next Tuesday and Wednesday with the king tides.
• A quick look at the dashboard between 4 and 9 AM Friday is enough; if the 1-hour burst alarm trips (0.40 in in one hour), move cars and watch the street.
• Expect cold mornings Friday and Saturday.
• Don't drive or walk through moving water.
